articles.description:
As a Computer Science student at Edinburgh Napier University, I was constantly frustrated with existing PDF tools. They were slow, expensive, or had annoying daily limits.
That's when I decided to build SnackPDF - a simple, pay-per-use PDF compression tool that actually works.
Existing tools have subscription models students can't afford
Daily limits are frustrating when you have assignments due
Most tools are slow and unreliable
Pay only when you use it (no subscriptions!)
Fast, reliable compression
Built by a real person, not a corporation
Building SnackPDF taught me that sometimes the best solutions come from personal frustration. When you're solving your own problem, you naturally build something better.
What PDF problems do you face? Let me know in the comments!
Try SnackPDF today: https://www.snackpdf.com
I'm Calum Kerr, a Computer Science student at Edinburgh Napier University building SnackPDF and RevisePDF. Follow my journey! 🚀

No cenário tecnológico atual, a figura do QA transcendeu a execução pura de testes. Hoje, falamos do Engenheiro de Qualidade: um profissional com atuação técnica, estratégica e profundamente colaborativa. Ele não apenas encontra bugs, mas os previne, influencia o design do produto e garante que a qualidade seja um ativo, e não um custo, para a empresa.

Este guia é seu mapa para construir e implementar uma matriz RACI eficaz, focada no Engenheiro de Qualidade e na realidade que o mercado exige.

🚀 A Hackathon Prototype for AIonRTX


This project was created as a submission to the NVIDIA G‑Assist Hackathon, where the goal is to build powerful plugins that extend the voice- and text-based capabilities of NVIDIA G‑Assist.
Our submission, SelfConfigAudit, explores a bold idea:
Can an AI agent reason about its own hardware configuration and determine whether it could autonomously modify it?
The answer—at least in this simulation—is a cautious "maybe."
SelfConfigAudit is a simulated G‑Assist plugin built in Python that mimics how an AI system might introspect, analyze, and evaluate its ability to modify NVIDIA GPU parameters such as:
Power limits

VRAM usage

Fan speed

CUDA cores

Core clocks



Importantly:  
⚠️ No actual hardware changes are made.
This project is a non-functional si…
articles.title: SelfConfigAudit – Simulating GPU Introspection in the Age of AI

articles.description:
Hey everyone 👋
About two months ago I posted about a real-time game I built called WWC Mafia — a quick, anonymous social deduction game inspired by Mafia/Werewolf that required no signup, just click and play.
Since then, I’ve kept building — and things got weird (in a good way 😄).
🧪 The Experiment Evolves
It’s not a product, not monetized — just an experimental multiplayer platform for fast, anonymous party games.
🕵️ What It Does
Lets you join party games (Mafia, Spyfall, Undercover) through secret links
🧰 Tech Stack
Frontend: Next.js + React
I like building things that feel alive — multiplayer, real-time, weird little online worlds.
Some of the goals for this were:
Push my understanding of WebSocket-based game loops
🔍 What I’m Still Exploring
Cleaner game logic across different party games
Real-time multiplayer is chaotic and rewarding
You can check out WWC Mafia here: (https://worldwidechat.vercel.app)
Thanks for reading. If you’re into multiplayer games, WebSocket stuff, or just weird online social projects — I’d love to see what you’re building too.
– Hito (aka H1-T0)
articles.title: I made a real-time Mafia game you can play with strangers – no signups(pt2)
